name: רְחוֹב
summary: Two men: Rehob the father of Hadadezer king of Zobah, whom David struck as he went to set up his monument at the river Euphrates (2Sa 8:3, 12); and a Levite who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day (Neh 10:12). The name is spelled as the noun רְחוֹב “open square”, and is also the name of towns in the north (Rehob, Beth-rehob), one of them Aramean, which may be behind the Aramean king's father's name. Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “David struck Hadadezer בֶּן־רְחֹב king of Zobah.”
“Mica, רְחוֹב, Hashabiah”, among the Levites who sealed.
Aram of Beth-rehob, hired with Aram of Zobah.
The noun the name is spelled as: the people gathered “into the square (הָרְחוֹב) before the Water Gate”.

note: No bdb key: the name's tokens are under t.bw.ag, which also holds the towns and several common-noun tokens and is kept on the place-name word רְחֹב in rachav.json (a key is in one entry or name only). TIPNR's Rehob@Neh.10.11 is Neh 10:12 in the Hebrew numbering.
